after_snippet:
# In pytest 9.0.0, overlapping arguments are automatically deduplicated
# pytest a/b a/ is equivalent to pytest a
# To get the old behavior of running tests twice, use --keep-duplicates

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    tmp = Path(tmpdir)
    
    # Create test structure
    (tmp / "a").mkdir()
    (tmp / "a" / "test_1.py").write_text("def test_a(): pass")
    (tmp / "a" / "b").mkdir()
    (tmp / "a" / "b" / "test_2.py").write_text("def test_b(): pass")
    
    # In 9.0.0, pytest a/b a/ is deduplicated to pytest a
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", "-q", "a/b", "a/"],
        cwd=tmp,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True
    )
    # Now this shows both tests (from a/ and a/b/)
    assert "2 test" in result.stdout
    
    # To get the old behavior of running duplicates:
    result2 = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", "-q", "--keep-duplicates", "a/b", "a/"],
        cwd=tmp,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True
    )
    # With --keep-duplicates, overlapping arguments are preserved
    assert result2.returncode == 0

# In pytest 8.4.2, pytest a/b a/ would only run tests in a/b
# and pytest x.py x.py would run the same file twice
# This behavior is no longer supported in 9.0.0

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    tmp = Path(tmpdir)
    
    # Create test structure
    (tmp / "a").mkdir()
    (tmp / "a" / "test_1.py").write_text("def test_a(): pass")
    (tmp / "a" / "b").mkdir()
    (tmp / "a" / "b" / "test_2.py").write_text("def test_b(): pass")
    
    # In 8.4.2, pytest a/b a/ would only discover tests in a/b
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", "-q", "a/b", "a/"],
        cwd=tmp,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True
    )
    # In 8.4.2 this would show only 1 test (from a/b)
    assert "1 test" in result.stdout
title: Overlapping and duplicate pytest arguments now deduplicate automatically
